content:
jdoe (Customer): Hey team — our users are stuck in a GitHub/Google login loop when coming from our marketing pages. Works if they open the app directly, but clicking the promo banner -> sign-in sometimes fails with 'state_mismatch' and they land back on /login. Only started this week.
maria (Support): Thanks — can you send an example URL (redact tokens) and whether it happens for both Google and GitHub? Any carrier/proxy in front of you?
jdoe (Customer): Example (redacted): https://app.example.com/auth/callback?code=***&state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.abc_def+ghi%3D--- it fails on GitHub more often, Google maybe 10% of attempts. Users come from marketing.example.com with UTM params.
maria (Support): Got it. Reproducing locally now. Which browsers affected?
jdoe (Customer): Chrome and Firefox mainly, Safari seems less common. Incognito sometimes works.
sanjeev (Eng): Quick theory: looks like the state is base64-url encoded JWT with dots and plus signs. If some middle proxy or tracker is re-encoding or converting '+' -> space or trimming after 2048 chars, the state won't match server-side stored value and we reject. Any chance the marketing banner adds long query (utm + campaign payload)?
jdoe (Customer): Yeah marketing adds utm_campaign and a big 'campaign_meta' param (long JSON blob). Could push URL length high.
maria (Support): Can you reproduce by clicking banner then login? If so please dump full redirect URL (headers fine to redact).
jdoe (Customer): Reproduced and pasted to support DM.
ashley (SRE): I checked ingress logs for the last hour — noticed several 301s from marketing host to app where querystring length got cut off. nginx shows "upstream sent too large header" around same timestamps for a handful of requests.
sanjeev (Eng): I pulled auth logs: we log the stored state as s_expected=eyJ... and when callback arrives we compare to s_returned=eyJ...; in failing cases s_returned is truncated (missing trailing "=%3D" or has spaces where '+' expected). Example failure log: "state mismatch: expected 'eyJhbGci..._abc+def==' got 'eyJhbGci..._abc def'". That matches plus->space normalisation.
maria (Support): That plus->space thing rings a bell — some proxies decode '+' to space when not using correct content type, or when query param isn't percent-encoded. Also some analytics middleware strips particular param names.
jdoe (Customer): Their marketing infra has a Fastly rule that rewrites URLs to add campaign_meta and also does an RFC3986-unsafe decode/encode for readability. They confirmed they recently rolled that rule.
sanjeev (Eng): Root cause hypothesis: campaign_meta injection + unsafe re-encoding at Fastly rewrites the querystring and converts '+' characters within the base64-url state into literal spaces, and sometimes truncates long querystrings leading to clipped state. Result: callback handler sees altered state -> rejects -> login loop.
maria (Support): Nice find. Any immediate mitigation for the customer while they fix Fastly rule?
sanjeev (Eng): Short-term options: 1) switch to storing a short random nonce as state (server maps nonce->JWT) so state is small and safe in querystring; 2) have marketing remove campaign_meta from redirect target or URL-encode their payload (encode '+' as %2B); 3) have users open app directly (not great). We can deploy a config toggle to use 'nonce-id' state in 24-48h.
ashley (SRE): Also can try increasing nginx buffer sizes on the app side but that won't fix '+'->space. Buffer tweak: proxy_buffer_size / large_client_header_buffers might avoid truncation but encoding issues remain.
jdoe (Customer): They can change Fastly rule quickly to url-encode special chars. I'll ask them to roll back within the hour. Meanwhile can you enable nonce-mode?
sanjeev (Eng): We'll prepare a temporary feature-flagged endpoint that issues a short 16-byte hex state instead of the full encoded JWT. Steps: make flag, update auth handler to accept nonce lookup, deploy to staging, smoke test with marketing flow. I can have a canary out in ~6 hours.
maria (Support): I'll coordinate with customer and Fastly contact. Please post requires QA steps and rollback plan here.
sanjeev (Eng): QA steps: 1) Deploy flag on staging, 2) hit marketing page -> click banner -> OAuth third-party -> callback, 3) verify state stored as short nonce and login completes, 4) confirm tokens issued and user session created. Rollback: flip flag off, old behavior restored.
ashley (SRE): Add monitoring: alert on auth callback failures > 1% and log sample mismatches. Also record raw querystring length distribution for diagnostics.
maria (Support): Customer update: marketing team rolled back Fastly rule and confirmed URLs now keep plus signs percent-encoded. They will also permanently URL-encode campaign_meta.
jdoe (Customer): Confirming — after rollback a subset of affected users can login again. Thanks for the quick turnaround.
sanjeev (Eng): Still going to push the nonce-mode toggle as defense-in-depth so future long campaign payloads don't break auth. I'll open a PR and link it here when ready.
maria (Support): Thanks everyone. I'll close the ticket once nonce-mode is live and customer confirms complete recovery. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for feature/short-nonce-auth at 2025-02-12T15:23:00Z
sanjeev (Eng): PR here: https://git.internal/r/redwood/auth/merge/789 — description: add feature flag AUTH_SHORT_STATE_NONCE, fallback to JWT state if off. Tests included.
maria (Support): Customer will test again tomorrow morning and confirm. If anything else crops up reopen ticket.
jdoe (Customer): All good for now — thanks!
